SOURCE-ASSISTED RECHECK — F-lwy7, 11 October 2026

Base: batch-2026-10-11-image-only. This is not a new independent reading. The reader now knows the catalogue subtitle identifying Exultet quotations and has seen search-result text from penitential works and an edition of a missal. None supplied a match for the containing work. Original first reading remains unchanged.

Resolution correction: the first packet was capped at 5000 pixels wide. Its native crops were native to that supplied image, not to the library original. This recheck uses library-native IIIF regions on canvas 1, fol. [1]v–[2]r, original size 7839×6347: (650,530,2900,1800) and (4230,3150,3150,1800). No rotation or filtering. They overlap the first reading's selected passages.

Image-002 line labels are retained from the base (first face/left column = fol. [1]v; right = fol. [2]r). These selected readings improve or qualify fragments but do not replace the base.

Left-column quotation and following prose:
L2: [illegible] O inestimabilis dilectio ca
L3: ritatis ut seruū redimeres? filiū tradidisti hic
L4: mirabilem? mutacione(m) rome? fontē? olei fluxit?
L5: in [crossed-out group, illegible] hora natiuitatis fluxit? [illegible]
L6: tota die? emanauit? [illegible] mirabilem?

The ending of redimeres is reconsidered after exposure to the known liturgical wording; redimeret in the first reading was not secure. Do not describe this correction as independent. Red underlining separates the quotation from the following explanation. The statement about an oil spring and the Nativity is connective material worth checking, but remains too uncertain for exact matching.

Right-column prose, selected portions only:
R18: Q(uando)? homo dolet de peccato suo et p(ro)p(ter) honore(m)
R19: dei [illegible; hole] [illegible] se offendisse [illegible]
R21: si sacerdos [illegible] dei et [illegible] ecclesie
R22: [illegible] p(ro)pter illud ad [illegible] confessione(m)
R24: [illegible] rubore postposito? pollicetur? de
R25: malis? illa est bona contricio De ista co(n)tricio(ne)?
R26: d(icitu)r? [illegible] Magna est velud mare [illegible]
R27: tua Istam contricione(m) habuit maria magdalē
R28: et beatus petrus [illegible]

The contrition/confession subject is supported, but these are incomplete model readings, not an expert checked transcript. Searches of the quoted liturgical line confirm an Exultet source layer only. Searches of surrounding oil-spring and contrition language yielded no sustained distinctive parallel; thematic parallels are not identifications. No containing author or work is established.
